subject: DPA addendum: subprocessor notification & objection process
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: DPA addendum: subprocessor notification & objection process

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking time on the DPA redline. Attached are two artifacts to start the subprocessor conversation: a proposed addendum (ACME_DPA_redline_20270314.pdf) and our current subprocessor register (subprocessor_list_v2.csv).

High-level ask from our side: we want a clear, operational notice + objection flow so both teams can add/remove subprocessors without repeated contract renegotiation. Proposed defaults in the addendum:
- Non-personal-data subprocessors: 30-day notice; if no objection within 30 days, processor is deemed accepted.
- Personal-data (PD) or high-risk subprocessors: 45-day notice and explicit acknowledgement required before onboarding.
- Standard objection template and a two-week mediation window once an objection is raised.

Can you confirm whether Acme can accept the deemed-acceptance clause for non-PD subprocessors? If not, please point us to the specific legal concerns so we can iterate.

We'd prefer to put the addendum through DocuSign once we land language. Link to a placeholder envelope will follow.

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0187

Attachments: ACME_DPA_redline_20270314.pdf (redline), subprocessor_list_v2.csv (current roster)
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmecloud.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA addendum: subprocessor notification & objection process

Sofia —

Thanks for the note and materials. We reviewed the addendum with our Legal Ops team. High level: we appreciate the operational approach but have a couple of non-negotiables from a privacy and procurement perspective.

Our positions:
- We cannot accept a blanket "deemed acceptance" for any subprocessors that will process personal data (PII or sensitive PD). For those processors, explicit written acceptance is required.
- 45-day notice for PD processors is our minimum.
- For non-PD tooling (e.g., CDN, monitoring of non-user telemetry), a 30-day notice with a default acceptance may be acceptable, subject to redlined language and the ability to escalate to our privacy team.

I've attached a short redline showing the language we'd insist on for the PD carve-out (see attached: ACME_legal_comments_20270315.pdf). If Redwood can commit to keeping PD processors to a short list and notify us with the PD classification, we can be flexible on non-PD timelines.

Also: please share a contact in your Privacy team who can answer a couple of quick questions about data residency for any new PD subprocessors.

Best,
Olivia
Olivia Chen
Enterprise Security & Privacy, AcmeCloud
olivia.chen@acmecloud.com

Attachment referenced: ACME_legal_comments_20270315.pdf
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA addendum: subprocessor notification & objection process (internal)

Team — quick internal summary and recommended stance based on Acme's reply:

Summary of Acme positions:
- 45 days and explicit acceptance required for any processor that handles personal data.
- 30 days + deemed acceptance likely acceptable for non-PD processors but they want the right to escalate.

Recommended Redwood stance (for internal approval):
1) Accept 45-day explicit acceptance for PD/high-risk subprocessors. We will label processors in our register with PD flag.
2) Offer 30-day notice with deemed-accept for non-PD processors. Deemed-accept limited to processors with a PD flag = false.
3) Add an escalation ladder:
   - Step 1: Customer raises objection in the template within the notice window.
   - Step 2: Technical review (we have 5 business days) — if issue resolvable (config, segregation), we fix it.
   - Step 3: If unresolved, hand to Legal (Monica) for remediation or substitution.
   - If still unresolved after 14 days, optional mediation clause kicks in.
4) Prepare two DocuSign addendum templates: one default (30/30) and one PD-locked (45/no-deem).

Action items: Monica, can you draft the customer-facing language for the addendum and the objection template? Aditya, we should align on whether sales credits or onboarding delays are appropriate concessions if a PD objection blocks a deal.

I've attached an internal risk matrix (internal_risk_matrix.xlsx) with suggested PD flags for the processors in the roster.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Director, Platform Partnerships (internal)
dev.patel@redwood.com
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA addendum: subprocessor notification & objection process

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the quick review and the redline. We discussed internally and are happy to accept Acme's PD carve-out as written with the following operational compromise so we can move forward without repeated contract churn: 

- Personal-data subprocessors: 45-day notice; explicit written acceptance required from Acme before onboarding (no deemed acceptance).
- Non-personal-data subprocessors: 30-day notice; if Acme does not raise an objection using the provided template within 30 days, the processor will be deemed accepted.
- Objection flow: customer must use the objection template (we'll include it in the addendum). Once an objection is received, Redwood will:
   1) Perform a 5-business-day technical remediation review;
   2) If remediation can't resolve the concern, escalate to Legal for negotiation (Monica will lead);
   3) If still unresolved after 14 days, both parties agree to a short mediation period to avoid onboarding delay.

We will produce two DocuSign addendum templates as Dev suggested: one default (30/30 deemed for non-PD) and one PD-locked (45/no-deem). For any processor marked PD in our register, the PD-locked flow will apply.

Please find a draft DocuSign envelope here for review and signature: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123

If this aligns with Acme's view, we'll send the addendum through DocuSign and include the objection form and a short guidance doc on how we classify PD vs non-PD processors.

Thanks and looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
